transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for the term-sheet review on the $60 million consumer receivable securitization. As is our standard process before I sign off, I need to hear from each of your areas — legal, credit risk, investor coverage, and loan operations. Please state any condition that must be reflected in the final term sheet before I can approve this transaction. We're looking at a four-year deal with a 2% reserve, a 5% delinquency trigger, monthly servicer remittances, and no special note-rating condition as currently drafted. Let's go around the table.

transcript.text: Maya, here are the contents of the legal memorandum I received this morning. Counsel can deliver a true-sale opinion only if two conditions are reflected in the final term sheet: first, the receivables must be transferred to a bankruptcy-remote special-purpose vehicle, and second, the seller must have no recourse for ordinary pool losses. Neither condition is currently reflected in the term sheet. I note that this memorandum has not yet been attached to the term-sheet file, but I am formally disclosing it now so these requirements can be incorporated before approval. I will ensure the memorandum is uploaded to the transaction room promptly.
